pages.title: Command Dispatch and Runtime Lifecycle
pages.purpose: How a `step` invocation travels from cmd/step/main.go through step.Init, the urfave/cli app, command registration, plugin fallback dispatch, and error/exit-code handling.
instructions: Cover exit codes, STEPDEBUG, panic handling, and the app.Action plugin fallback explicitly.

pages.title: Architecture Overview
pages.purpose: High-level architecture of the step CLI: binary surface, module layout, package ownership boundaries, and how command groups relate to supporting packages.
instructions: Describe ownership boundaries (command/, flags/, token/, utils/, internal/, pkg/) without narrating every file.

pages.title: Shared Flags and Configuration
pages.purpose: The flags package: reusable flag definitions, CA URL/root resolution, password sourcing rules, and the precedence between flags, defaults.json, and prompts.
instructions: State precedence rules only where the source establishes them.

pages.title: STEPPATH and Contexts
pages.purpose: The STEPPATH filesystem layout (defaults.json, contexts.json, profiles/authorities) and the context model for switching between authorities.
instructions: Explain when contexts are enabled and what files are written where; cite source for each path.

pages.title: CA Bootstrap Flow
pages.purpose: End-to-end bootstrap flow: resolving team/authority data, downloading and pinning the root certificate, writing defaults.json, creating contexts, and optional truststore installation.
instructions: Trace both BootstrapTeamAuthority and BootstrapAuthority variants.

pages.title: Certificate Renewal and Lifecycle
pages.purpose: Certificate lifecycle operations: `step ca renew`, rekey, revoke, and needs-renewal; mTLS vs token authentication, daemon mode with jitter, --exec/--pid reload hooks, and the shipped systemd units.
instructions: Document the renewal timing model (2/3 validity, --expires-in, --renew-period) as established by the source.

pages.title: OAuth and Single Sign-On
pages.purpose: The `step oauth` command: OAuth2/OIDC authorization code, out-of-band, device authorization, JWT bearer, and refresh token flows, including the local redirect server and output modes.
instructions: Cite the default client IDs and flow selection logic; avoid inventing provider behavior beyond the source.

pages.title: SSH Certificates
pages.purpose: The `step ssh` command group: user/host certificate issuance, login/logout with the SSH agent, config generation, check-host, proxycommand, and hosts discovery.
instructions: Note SSH-specific token types and agent interactions.

pages.title: Token Generation
pages.purpose: How step builds and signs JWT tokens for the CA: claim defaults, audience derivation per token type, provisioner selection, and the shared token flow used by ca commands.
instructions: Cover token types (Sign/Revoke/SSH*/Renew), audiences, and validity bounds.

pages.title: X.509 Certificate Issuance
pages.purpose: The `step ca certificate`/`step ca sign` issuance flow from flags to a signed certificate, including the online sign API call and the offline CA mode.
instructions: Explain when offline mode is used and how it differs from the online flow.

pages.title: Guide: Adding a Command
pages.purpose: Focused change guide: register a new command or subcommand, reuse shared flags, follow error/prompt conventions, and wire it into the binary.
instructions: Base every step on the documented registration pattern in command/README.md and an existing simple command.

pages.title: Guide: Extending CA Flows
pages.purpose: Focused change guide for maintenance on the CA flows: where token types, audiences, clients, and offline mode must be kept consistent, and which tests to run before merging.
instructions: Frame as invariants and checkpoints; avoid prescribing changes the source does not support.

pages.title: CA Client Integration
pages.purpose: The CaClient abstraction: online step-ca client construction, the offline CA wrapper (singleton authority), and the admin API client including on-the-fly admin certificate issuance.
instructions: Explain the offline singleton rationale and flag requirements exactly as coded.

pages.title: KMS and Plugin Integrations
pages.purpose: Plugin architecture: step-<name>-plugin discovery and execution, the built-in step-kms-plugin integration via internal/cryptoutil, KMS URI detection, and TPM attestation support.
instructions: Distinguish the exec-based plugin fallback from the go-step-sm/kms library integration.

pages.title: Build, Release, and Packaging
pages.purpose: Building and shipping step: Makefile targets, GoReleaser Pro build matrix and nfpm packages, Docker images, debian packaging, systemd units, shell autocomplete, and the release workflow.
instructions: State which artifacts each mechanism produces; flag uncertainty where config is Pro-only.

pages.title: Testing and CI
pages.purpose: How the repository is tested: unit tests with gotestsum, testscript-based integration tests, coverage, race mode, and the CI workflow that gates merges.
instructions: List the actual test entry points and what each level covers.

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.purpose: Task-oriented entry point: build the step binary, run tests, and see where to go next for architecture, flows, and change guides.
instructions: Keep quickstart practical and short; route readers to the deeper pages rather than duplicating them.
